title: Glutamate measurement
author: Karen Maciel de Oliveira

steps_raw.instruction: Glutamate measurement Material: 1. 22G needle 2. 1 ml syringe 3. Cold chamber 4. Cerebrospinal fluid sample 5. NADP+ (final concentration 1.0 mM) 6. CaCl2 (final concentration 1.0 mM) 7. Glutamate dehydrogenase (50 units) 8. Glutamate (final concentration 1 mM) Procedures: 1. Immediately after euthanasia, the rat head is flexed downward at approximately 45º, to reveal a palpable depressible surface with the appearance of a rhomb between the occipital protuberances and the spine of the atlas. 2. The 22G needle is inserted in the cisterna magna for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection and connected to a 1 -mL syringe. Then, 50 -80 µL of non -contaminated sample is drawn into the syringe by simple and careful aspiration, and maintained in a refrigerator -80ºC. 3. Transfer the CSF to the housing of the fluorimeter, and fluorescence at 450 nm is recorded after excitation at 360 nm. Then immediately, add NADP+ (final concentration 1.0 mM), follow by CaCl2 (final concentration 1.0 mM). 4. After a further 70s period, add glutamat e dehydrogenase (50 units) and monitor NADPH+ fluorescence allowed until reaching the equilibrium state, visualizing as a constant fluorescence value, made to measure the glutamate in different samples (5µL). 5. Subsequently, after 500s period, perform the c alibration by adding standard glutamate (final concentration 1mM) to the system. 6. Results are described as nmol/µL of CSF to the maximum response obtained with the final addition of 1mM of glutamate. References:
